notes.title: Unpacking is available now on mobile & tablets!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/45b0432d233d5099132f6c8b3733c0d5ecc38740.jpg[/img]

[h2]Today’s the day! Unpacking is officially available on the App Store and Google Play! [/h2]

[url=https://apps.apple.com/us/app/unpacking/id6450058135][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/385e8b1eb8958e609bf329318cc24c7e8c2e76d3.png[/img][/url]

[url=https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.humblebundle.unpacking][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/8237d8ce39628d42b01b46fcffd5769fe56f70f4.png[/img][/url]

We’ll keep this post short and sweet because the important information is right there—Unpacking is now available on mobile and tablets, and you can purchase it at the links above.

A few FAQs for those curious: 
[list]
[*] You can play it on BOTH phones and tablets
[*] It is a premium title, but the price may vary based on what country you’re in.
[*] There are no ads or in-app purchases!
[*] It's the complete game – now designed to play great with touch screen controls right in the palm of your hand!
[/list]
We hope you enjoy it in its new form, and please tag us ([url=https://twitter.com/UnpackingALife]@UnpackingALife[/url] on Twitter and [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@unpackinggame]@unpackinggame[/url] on TikTok) if you take any particularly good photos or videos of you playing it out in the world. We’d love to see them!

notes.title: Unpacking is coming to mobile & tablets!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/26ca40b9945cf115306b7688efc44be903ad3dd8.jpg[/img]

[h2]We’ve got news to share![/h2]
[b]We have an announcement coming up[/b]—we're coming to phones and tablets later this year!  

[url=https://wholesomegames.com/]Wholesome Direct[/url] is a yearly celebration of exclusive footage and announcements from 70+ indie games, [b]and this year, that includes Unpacking![/b] As a heads up, it’s not a DLC announcement, [b]but it’s still something that a lot of folks have been asking for![/b]

And a quick little post-Wholesome Direct edit to say—our news is that [b]we're coming to mobile and tablets![/b] We're so excited about this, and you can [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1135690/announcements/detail/3674421166713919914]see the full announcement here[/url]! 

[h2]In other news...[/h2]

[url=https://twitter.com/alxxjms/status/1665063494436155393][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/43bac676386d9f1759e401f0043b4bdbaa26a594.jpg[/img][/url]
More beautiful fanart by [url=https://twitter.com/alxxjms/status/1665063494436155393]alxxjms[/url]

Disegno published a really lovely piece on Unpacking—hitting points about the expansiveness and limits of cozy and wholesome games as a genre, the sadness we can feel when comparing our life to that of a protagonist, and the stories that are told throughout Unpacking. It’s well worth a read! 

[url=https://store.serenityforge.com/collections/unpacking-collection][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/b34a55169de13941c852a91da7cfe4a57590b531.jpg[/img][/url]

Don’t forget, Unpacking merchandise and plushies [url=https://store.serenityforge.com/collections/unpacking-collection]are still available at Serenity Forge![/url] We absolutely love seeing them come to life, and as shipments are arriving at folks’ homes, it’s brought us so much joy! 

See you all Saturday at Wholesome Direct! 

Cheers,

Emily & the Unpacking team

notes.title: How Unpacking handles sentimentality, level design, “stuff” and the idea of home
notes.content:
Two great interviews, one with Edge Magazine and one with Gameshub, that we’re quite proud of! 

We [url=https://www.gamesradar.com/the-making-of-unpacking-developer-witch-beam-on-bringing-the-moving-indie-hit-to-life/]talked to [b]Edge[/b] about a huge range of things[/url], from choosing which items came along from each level, sentimentality, level design of the post-boyfriend level, UI/interface, and of course: fan theories. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/5607fcc6aecb03c9c124588d5e3bfbccf432c0c2.png[/img]

[url=https://www.gameshub.com/news/features/unpacking-tim-dawson-wren-brier-interview-homes-as-reflective-human-places-39165/]With [b]Gameshub[/b][/url], the conversation began with our definitions of home, and then we discussed the idea of “stuff” in the game, what you can control (and what you can’t), and how the ways people play the game is still so, so varied. 

[h3]We’re headed to GDC! [/h3]
It’s a month out (how is that possible?) and we’re headed to GDC to give two talks. Please come join us if you’re attending the conference! 

[b]Wren[/b] will be giving a talk about building a game in a way that defies many game design mechanics, and why they made these choices, called [url=https://schedule.gdconf.com/session/unpacking-zen-designing-a-game-without-fail-states-or-scores/892873][b]'Unpacking' Zen: Designing a Game Without Fail States or Scores[/b][/url] on Wednesday, March 22nd at 2-3:00 PM PT

[b]Emily[/b] (that’s me!) will be giving a talk on social media and marketing a game after its launch, and how to maintain momentum, called [url=https://schedule.gdconf.com/session/independent-games-summit-unpacking-fan-expectations-and-driving-engagement-post-launch/892023][b]'Unpacking' Fan Expectations and Driving Engagement Post-Launch[/b][/url] on Tuesday, March 21 at 1:20-1:50 PM PT

[h3]Don’t forget! [/h3]
Unpacking physical editions are still available at major retailers ([url=https://amzn.to/3EcXFMx]Amazon[/url], [url=https://bit.ly/3hqv4up]Target[/url], and others!) and you can still pick up Unpacking merchandise from [url=https://store.serenityforge.com/collections/unpacking-collection]Serenity Forge’s online shop[/url]. We’ve been loving seeing people share their pictures of packages arriving! 

Also, we’ve been posting some [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@unpackinggame/video/7196032687377894657]looks behind the scenes[/url]—as well as some [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@unpackinggame/video/7203831520589597953]creative interpretations of what people think some of the items are[/url]—on TikTok, so join us there if you’re interested!

Cheers, 

Emily & the Witch Beam team

notes.title: Taking a deep dive into Unpacking’s sound & design
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/e77531ae7f782164cc00579e7210cfbeb018d2a3.png[/img]
[b]Above[/b]: [i][url=https://twitter.com/beezelbee_/status/1548805514548633604]@beezelbee_[/url] is building the 1997 room in miniature, and we’re loving following the process[/i]

Hello Unpacking fans! It’s been a busy month, but at this point, maybe there’s no such thing as a slow month! 

[h2]ABC Australia Mini Doco[/h2]
We’re very excited that this mini-doco has come out—[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OiEg4brhXUA]ABC Australia came to Wren and Tim’s apartment[/url] on the day of the game launch, and it’s crazy to think about how far we’ve come since this day in November.

[previewyoutube=OiEg4brhXUA;full][/previewyoutube]

We also got reminded that we made our Twitter account four years ago, and it’s resulted in some nostalgia as we think about where we were at that time—at [url=http://www.stugan.com/]Stugan[/url], in Sweden, building out ovens and taking the first pass at the 1997 level! Wild to see all that progress. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/ec92030528b30cbb3f11a08d7676b2232009fd16.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/d772b2006c1855ce77e44774dfdfdf8cf15e9ed4.jpg[/img]

[h2]Listen & Learn[/h2]
Jeff & Ange have been giving some great behind-the-scenes looks at the sound design behind Unpacking. First up, [url=https://www.patreon.com/posts/68826094]they were on [b]Level with Emily Reese[/b][/url] to talk about sound, music and the complications of recording foley for the game, and then followed that up with [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VnoK2OKF-dQ&t=12827s]a video as part of [b]Save & Sound[/b][/url], which dives into the environmental ambiance of the levels (listen for a school letting out at around 3PM in the first level!), how they tracked the sounds of objects across different surfaces. And keep in mind there’s variations on each sound as well! 

We put together [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@unpackinggame/video/7120658471015435521]a TikTok of some of our favorite sounds—what’s yours? 
[/url]

[h2]Another peek[/h2]
On the other end of things (narrative and game design, that is!) Wren & Tim have had a few chances to take some deep dives as well. [url=https://blog.playstation.com/2022/07/01/official-playstation-podcast-episode-435-unpacking-retro-origins/][b]The PlayStation podcast[/b] had them on[/url] to talk about different playstyles, hidden details (if you shake the PS5 controller, it shakes the item!), and telling narratives in unique ways. Then, [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-zaVo2KdMIk&]on an episode of [b]Noclip[/b][/url], they talked about all the systems behind the game, and the video is a great look at the game being built in Unity as well as the grids on each level for item placement!

[previewyoutube=-zaVo2KdMIk;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]We’re headed to BitSummit! [/h2]
So excited to announce that we’re headed to [url=https://bitsummit.org/en/]BitSummit X-Roads[/url] this year! We showed Unpacking at BitSummit in 2019, and we’re so glad to be headed back. If you’ll be there—let us know! 

[h2]Easter Egg found! [/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/cebcaa179127dedf48d567bb7a3b60172876f1cb.jpg[/img]
We’re delighted to say that the easter egg from last month’s newsletter has been found! It’s found by interacting with the game console in the 2015 level—and is [b]Witch Beam’s next game, TemPoPo![/b] 

That’s all for this month! Next month brings BitSummit and Wren’s keynote at NZGDC, and we can’t wait to share both with you! 

Cheers, 

Emily & the Witch Beam Team

notes.title: Five great reads, two deep dive videos, and one easter egg
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/040155cb64e9a160ab5c04fc86c546e568fc2988.jpg[/img]
[i]top row and bottom left: Karoliina Korhonen / bottom right: [url=https://twitter.com/mvambrosoni?lang=en]María Ambrosoni[/url][/i]

We are loving these Sims 4 builds that have recreated some of the apartments from Unpacking! If you are so inspired, please share with us on our [url=https://discord.gg/unpacking ]Discord[/url] or on [url=https://twitter.com/UnpackingALife]Twitter[/url]! 

[h2]Game maker’s notebook[/h2]
ICYMI, we’ve had two different sessions with the Game Maker’s Notebook, one with Jeff about sound and music, and one with Tim and Wren about narrative, how the game came about, and more. Check ‘em out! 

[h2]Some great reads[/h2]
There have been some great articles recently about Unpacking, and we wanted to share them: 
[list]
[*] [url=https://i-d.vice.com/en_uk/article/7kbj54/unpacking-bisexual-video-game][b]How a video game about unpacking gets the bisexual experience spot on[/b][/url] | i-D magazine dives into streamers’ reactions to the final levels of the game and how important that representation feels to experience in a game.
[*] [url=https://www.eurogamer.net/how-unpackings-art-combines-beauty-with-clarity][b]How Unpacking's art combines beauty with clarity[/b][/url] | Eurogamer talked with our artist, Angus Doolan about creating isometric designs that can be readable, tell a story, and fit within the mechanics of the game
[*] [url=https://www.eurogamer.net/the-creators-of-unpacking-on-developing-a-weird-queer-bafta-winning-game][b]The creators of Unpacking on developing a "weird", queer, BAFTA-winning game[/b][/url] | Wren and Tim sat down with Eurogamer to discuss mechanics, level design combined with storytelling, showing the many facets of the protagonist, the surprise reach of the game, and more. 
[*] [url=https://blog.playstation.com/2022/05/06/objects-tell-stories-in-unpacking-arriving-on-ps4-and-ps5-may-10/][b]Objects tell stories in Unpacking[/b][/url] | Tim wrote a piece for the PlayStation blog about the real-life inspiration for items in the game 
[*] [url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-04-15/unpacking-brisbane-baftas-game-of-the-year-best-narrative-/100992020][b]Meet the Brisbane couple who claimed two major prizes at the BAFTA Game Awards[/b][/url] | It’s been very surreal to have our local news come and interview us! 
[/list]
[h2]The G.A.N.G. Awards[/h2]
Making room on our shelf for two more awards—this time from the Game Audio Network Guild! We won [b]Best Sound Design for an Indie Game[/b] and [b]Best Audio for an Indie Game[/b], and we’re really proud to be recognized among an incredible slate. You can see the full list of winners here. 

[h2]A little easter egg to find…[/h2]
A pixel art rendition of the key art for our next game exists somewhere inside Unpacking, and no one has found it yet! Let us know if you find it! 

Cheers, 

Emily & the Witch Beam team

notes.title: Vote for us in the Webbys & check out our GDC talks!
notes.content:
Hello all and happy April! It’s been a very busy month for us, and it’s not over yet! First up, we’re nominated for [b]FOUR Webby Awards[/b], and would greatly appreciate if you could send a few votes our way. We’re right on the cusp of winning for two in particular, so click here to vote: [url=https://vote.webbyawards.com/PublicVoting#/2022/games/general-games/family-kids][b]Family & Kids[/b][/url], and [url=https://vote.webbyawards.com/PublicVoting#/2022/games/features/best-user-experience][b]Best User Experience[/b][/url]. Voting closes TOMORROW, so don't delay!

[h3][b]Still time to pre-order[/b][/h3]
Also you still have time to get your pre-orders in for [url=https://limitedrungames.com/collections/unpacking]Physical Editions of Unpacking[/url] as well as the [url=https://limitedrungames.com/collections/unpacking/products/unpacking-2lp-vinyl-soundtrack]soundtrack on vinyl[/url]! Pre-orders end [b]May 1st[/b], so don’t hesitate! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/e3462d32371c303e7dc1f56a96e9797ed046ca16.jpg[/img]

[h3]Have you played Dark Star Mode yet? [/h3]
Our favorite part of this month, though, was announcing our favorite secret about the game: Dark Star Mode. [url=https://twitter.com/UnpackingALife/status/1509919950806274053]We announced it on April 1st[/url], and somehow people thought we were joking! Imagine that… 😉  [b]Dark Star Mode is real[/b], and the only tips we’ll give you are these: make sure to start a new album, and remember that everything has to be in the wrong place: including things you haven’t unpacked! If you can move it, it must be moved! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/eb11edb721fa3f876ec09cf92790248e667a804c.jpg[/img]

[h3]GDC talks online[/h3]
GDC has passed behind us, and you can now watch and read our talks! [url=https://www.gdcvault.com/play/1027728/-Unpacking-The-Fun-Behind]Jeff’s full talk on all things foley[/url] is here—and available for everyone!—and you can also [url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/gdc2022/auditory-tales-from-the-making-of-zen-puzzler-unpacking]read a summary on Game Developer[/url]. For a look at Wren and Tim’s talk about narrative, you can also [url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/gdc2022/gdc-2022-unpacking-a-narrative-through-1-000-household-items]check it out on Game Developer.[/url]

[h3]We’re on cloud nine… [/h3]
In the space of a few weeks, we won two [url=https://gdconf.com/news/inscryption-wins-game-year-gdca-2022]GDCA Awards[/url], Best Audio and the Innovation Award, and then at the [url=https://www.bafta.org/games/awards/2022-nominations-winners]BAFTA Game Awards[/url], we won Best Narrative and EE Game of the Year (thank you to everyone who voted to help make that happen!) At the BAFTAs, you might have seen that we were so surprised, [url=https://twitter.com/BAFTAGames/status/1513463673259503619]we didn’t have a speech planned[/url] 😬  but we realized after it was [url=https://twitter.com/UnpackingALife/status/1514950044533030919]a great chance to thank everyone involved[/url] once we’d caught our breath a little. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/90d26b4129c00242874617943870d1b49304b691.jpg[/img]

That’s all for now, and as always, follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/UnpackingALife]Twitter[/url] for even more news, join our [url=https://discord.gg/unpacking]Discord[/url] to chat with other fans, and follow us on [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@unpackinggame]TikTok[/url] for fun videos. 

Cheers, 

Emily & the Witch Beam team

notes.title: Additional language support
notes.content:
This update adds five additional languages, and addresses some bugs and small issues we've had reported.

[list]
[*] Language support for Italian, Turkish, Indonesian, Filipino and Malay languages - where possible the game will use the language specified in your Steam client, but it's always been possible to set your preferred language in game from the Settings menu on the Title Screen
[*] Fixed a disappearing text issue that was affecting some MacOS and Linux users
[*] Fixed various small issues
[*] Made some adjustments to item validation based on player feedback
[/list]
We've also had reports that some Mac users are receiving warnings that Unpacking has been blocked because it may reduce privacy and lower security. As this did not coincide with a game update we're not sure what caused this change.

Unpacking does not track or transmit user data (beyond anything required for Steam to function) but we do not recommend anyone disregard the safety messages of their operating system. If this update doesn't improve the situation we will continue to investigate.

notes.title: Thank You 💜 Unpacking Post-Launch and Awards!
notes.content:
Hi Unpackers!

Wow, it’s been a wild month since we released Unpacking on November 2nd. During that time you smashed ALL of our expectations – we climbed the top of the Nintendo Switch charts globally, were featured on Steam’s front page, and so much more. But even more than that, we got to see how much you all loved and connected with our game. Whether it was the diploma moment, the tears, or the discovery of our 14,000 foley audio sounds, you were just as vulnerable and overjoyed as we felt making this.

From the entire team, thank you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/31321e5f520c2c8e0900afa942843782a12fae83.png[/img]

[h1]Press Round Up[/h1]
Unpacking seemed to be overall loved by various news outlets, and it was real cool seeing our little puzzle game up there with some big names. If you’re interested, we highlighted them over on [url=https://witchbeam.com.au/2021/12/08/thank-you-%f0%9f%92%9c-unpacking-post-launch-and-awards/]our blog[/url].

[h1]Voting, Community Wiki, and What’s Next[/h1]
It’s still awards season, which means if you enjoyed our game you can help it win some pretty cool accolades! (And then the next time we move, we can awkwardly try and pack the trophies into boxes. If they even come with trophies???)

You can vote for us to win the [url=https://caniplaythat.com/2021/12/04/can-i-play-that-accessibility-awards-2021-voting-begins/]Can I Play That? Accessibility Awards[/url] – Indie Excellence & Best Cognitive Accessibility. If you feel Unpacking deserves any of these, it would mean so much if you would nominate Unpacking. It only takes a few clicks to do so, and it would mean so much to us!

Meanwhile, for those who have been stuck or wanted to discover all the secrets of the game, our lovely Discord community has started an [url=https://unpacking.fandom.com/wiki/Unpacking_Wiki]unofficial Unpacking fan wiki[/url], which you can see here.

As for the most frequently asked question we’ve gotten so far… Will there be more content?! We love how much the game has connected with people, but we don’t currently have plans to make additional content. We are really happy with the arc of the game. It’s not the biggest story, but we liked how things finished. Stories start and end, boxes are unpacked, and it’s ok to feel settled. It’s why we spent so long (3.5 years!) working on it — we didn’t want to cut anything we planned. There is a lot of story hidden in the items and environments. If you enjoyed the game, you can always play through again and see what else you can learn about the characters and story. (Only a few people have discovered one of the biggest secrets..!) Basically: we truly appreciate the love and community behind this game. Not wanting to add more content isn’t a sign that we don’t care! We want to respect our game and story, and not try to arbitrarily add to it. For now we’re done, but the future holds many mysteries. If you’d like, you can follow the game’s creative director [url=https://twitter.com/Wrenegadey]Wren on Twitter[/url] to see what she gets up to, after she takes a well deserved break.

[h1]Notes about scams[/h1]
It’s come to our attention there are a number of scam Unpacking apps on the Google Play store. To clarify: Unpacking is NOT available on mobile, and there are currently no plans to port it to mobile. We’re sorry for any disappointment!

Whew!

That’s it for now. Hope you all have a good holiday and rest of your year! 2022 has a lot of mystery to it, but if our game has taught us anything… There are plenty of good things to unpack.

Cheers,

Victoria, Wren, and the Witch Beam team

notes.title: Fixes and updates
notes.content:
This update addresses an issue that could prevent the game starting if the window had been moved to a second monitor along with some other minor issues.
[list]
[*] In some cases, moving the game window to a second monitor that had a different scaling factor to the default monitor would prevent the game from restarting. Previously we were advising workarounds but this should no longer be a problem
[*] When VSync was disabled, the game was capable of excessive CPU usage. A maximum framerate has been set for when the game is run without vsync
[*] fixed an issue involving drawers that are above doors that could allow incorrect item placement in 2007, 2013 and 2015
[*] fixed a couple of minor visual issues
[/list]
Save files and progress should be unaffected.

if you have rebound your controls in a way that makes navigating the menus difficult, it's possible to reset them now from outside the game by adding

[b]resetcontrols[/b]

to [b]Launch Options[/b]. Remember to remove this text once you've customised your controls or they will be reset each time you start the game!

notes.title: Fixes and updates
notes.content:
This update addresses an input rebinding issue and fixes some smaller issues and placement rules
[list]
[*] Input rebinding allowed binding the esc key over the primary action input, resulting in menus that couldn't be navigated. This is now prevented and if you had bound it this way the game will revert your input bindings on start
[*] fixed a Steam integration issue that was blocking progression in rare cases
[*] fixed issue where items could be placed in the corner of a shower and not retrieved
[*] fixed issue that occasionally caused items in drawers to be very hard to select if there was an item on the floor behind them
[*] fixed a "vanishing book" issue caused by holding a book over a shelf while changing rooms
[*] added a missing sprite to a toothpaste in 2012 and fixed issue where an item in 2018 could be hung on hooks and towel racks when it wasn't meant to be
[*] tweaked the dining-room reverb in 2007
[*] fixed an issue that was causing red validation outlines to render with visual artefacts on specific screen resolutions
[*] several items have had some extra areas assigned to them either because they should have been that way originally or we saw it in someone's stream and were like "yeah, fair"
[*] fixed other various visual issues
[/list]
Save files and progress should be unaffected.

Features and improvements
[list]
[*] Big Picture mode now uses a virtual keyboard when naming your album
[*] the pulsing button effect that signals that other rooms have unpacked boxes has been reduced slightly
[/list]
The pulsing can also be turned off entirely by adding

[b]nopulse[/b]

to [b]Launch Options[/b] - this is considered a workaround and will hopefully have an in-game menu option in future.

Thank you for playing!

notes.title: ✨ Unpacking is out now! ✨
notes.content:
Unpackers!

It's finally here.

[h2]Unpacking is out now on Steam![/h2]

[previewyoutube=vPcoMltTVXE;full][/previewyoutube]

Unpacking is a zen game about the familiar experience of pulling possessions out of boxes and fitting them into a new home. Part block-fitting puzzle, part home decoration, you are invited to create a satisfying living space while learning clues about the life you’re unpacking. Over the course of eight house moves, you are given a chance to experience a sense of intimacy with a character you never see and a story you’re never told. After 3 years of development, we're so excited to finally share our cozy game with the world! We hope you love it as much as we do.

There are a ton of ways you can help us out other than just buying the game too. Especially for a small indie studio, we also appreciate things like:
[list]
[*] Spreading the word to family, friends, and even your favorite streamer
[*] Leaving a review on Steam
[*] Sharing our news on social media
[/list]
But no pressure - we're grateful to have you here at all!

[h2]Share Your Rooms![/h2]

A fun new feature of the game is our built-in playback and GIF maker feature. This allows you to easily capture and share your unpacking process with the community.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/1455dd2b529b34e0017b6a7fee1a529d0954abcb.gif[/img]

One of our favorite things is seeing your creativity and organizational skills shine. Please feel free to tag us on [url=https://twitter.com/UnpackingALife]Twitter @UnpackingALife[/url] if you end up using the feature. You can also tag us if you stream the game - we might even pop in and say hi!

[h2]AMAs[/h2]

Finally, if you end up having any burning questions about our development process or Unpacking in general, we have two AMAs lined up. You can catch us on either:
[list]
[*] Nov 3, 5pm PST on [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/nintendoswitch]r/NintendoSwitch[/url]
[*] Nov 9, 6pm PST on [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/girlgamers]r/GirlGamers[/url]
[/list]
And of course, you can also join our community over on [url=https://discord.gg/unpacking]Discord[/url] if you're looking for like-minded unpackers.

Whew, that's all for now. Happy unpacking, and thanks again from all of us at Witch Beam!

Cheers,

Wren, Victoria, and the Witch Beam team

notes.title: Game of the Year and Excellence in Accessibility Awards!
notes.content:
Hey Unpackers!

We were honored to have won TWO important awards at the [url=https://twitter.com/The_AGDAs/status/1445682031602507782?s=20]Australian Game Developer Awards[/url] this year for Unpacking: Excellence in Accessibility and Game of the Year!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35621891/8925b41cdbaee5e54bfcb63a9b4b8d34f61fe67d.png[/img]

It means a lot to have Unpacking recognised for its accessibility. With no timers and no fail states we felt we had already created a game with a broad potential audience so it became even more important to be as inclusive as possible. Whenever we put the demo in front of someone and they mentioned something they struggled with that we had not intended to be a struggle, we looked into what we could do to improve their experience and in some cases implement settings to adapt the game to their needs. Games should be for everyone!

As for winning Game of the Year… wow! We’re honoured to receive this award, especially given the incredible games we were up against. Unpacking is such a personal project for us — the idea came about when two of our team members moved in together, and we’ve all put a lot of ourselves into the game. It’s amazing how it’s resonated with so many of you!

The biggest thanks to all of you in the community for having our back, providing feedback, and just sharing the game with your friends. It’s done so much for us, and we hope to make you proud!

[h2]Last Notes[/h2]
The rest of the month is going to be as hectic as ever, so please make sure you wishlist the game! And for those wondering about the price, we can confirm it’ll be $19.99 USD on all platforms. Hope the clarifies any lingering questions about the game.

See you in less than a month!

Cheers,
Victoria and the Unpacking team

—

notes.title: Demo update #2
notes.content:
Another minor update! Don't mind us!

Changes include:
[list]
[*] The sound the Star makes when you put everything in valid places no longer plays repeatedly if you keep moving things about - we were watching people stream the demo and it got super annoying, honestly it's the only reason we're doing this update
[*] esc button on the main menu will skip the logo sequence for people who are in a hurry to play our extremely chill slow paced game
[/list]

notes.title: Demo update
notes.content:
We've released a minor quality of life update to the Unpacking demo!

Changes include:
[list]
[*] Made the "Witch Beam" whisper quieter so it's not as scary
[*] Added control-click for turning items for our one button Mac mouse friends
[*] Several items have been marked up to be allowed in more places
[*] Caught an issue where the game might not auto save if you quit too quickly
[*] Fixed issue where room icons could show up wrong on load
[*] Escape key no longer immediately quits from the main menu
[/list]

If you've already successfully played through the demo these changes are unlikely to give you a different experience but we're hopeful they'll make things a little bit nicer for anyone who checks it out between now and the end of PAX.

But of course you can play it again if you'd like, that's totally allowed.
